title: Manatee Solar Energy Center: Phase 56I First-Pass Decision
summary: EIA's July 23 release extends the official EIA-923 rail through May 2026 and describes monthly and annual plant- and prime-mover-level generation data. Phase 56I decision: No closure change. Monthly plant operations are a stronger acquisition rail, but the release contract does not supply Manatee interval dispatch, availability, state of charge, cycling, or degradation.
key_findings: Highest-value missing record: Interval dispatch and availability for the named battery.
Continuation rule: Reopen when FPL, Florida PSC, EIA, or a balancing authority publishes asset-specific operating data with a declared interval and availability denominator.
why_it_matters: The first-pass decision records whether a named official rail supplies the required denominator without converting adjacent or partial evidence into false closure.
ftfn_relevance: Completes the Phase 56I first-pass queue under a dated source check.
Keeps evidence state separate from performance, safety, quality, readiness, and value.
evidence_limits: The release page describes monthly and annual survey data; it does not itself establish a Manatee interval series, availability, state of charge, cycling, degradation, revenue, or customer outcome.
Interval dispatch, availability, cycles, state of charge, degradation, revenue, curtailment, outage response, and customer cost.
No causal effect, ranking, composite score, readiness score, or unsupported cross-entity comparison is supported.
